Transmission and Seeding over the Historical Period

Source: R/transmission_history.R
build_transmission_history.Rd

Builds the time-varying basic reproduction number and the seeded infections for a historical run, under a stated assumption about how reported cases relate to true infections.

Usage

build_transmission_history(
  case_reports,
  population,
  years,
  R0,
  disease,
  transmission_history = c("circulating_years", "reported_cases_only"),
  circulation_threshold = 2,
  reporting_fraction = 1,
  seed_floor = 10
)

Arguments

case_reports

Data frame of WHO case reports for one country and disease, with columns `year` and `cases`. Years with zero reported cases should be included; missing reports can be `NA` or absent.

population

Matrix of population (thousands) by year (rows, in the order of `years`) and single year of age (columns).

years

Model years.

R0

Basic reproduction number while transmission is on.

disease

Disease name.

transmission_history

The reporting assumption (see above).

circulation_threshold

Reported cases per million people per year at or above which the disease is taken to be circulating. Default 2.

reporting_fraction

Share of infections that are reported (default 1).

seed_floor

Minimum number of infections introduced each year under `"circulating_years"` (default 10).

Value

A list with `R0` and `tt_R0` (days), `seed_data` (long format, by single year of age), `tt_seeded` (days), and `summary`, a data frame by year of reported cases, seeded infections and whether transmission was on.

Reporting assumptions

WHO case reports badly under-count infections in most settings, but how badly is not known. Until reporting fractions are estimated (for example from seroprevalence surveys) the history has to be run under an assumption, chosen with `transmission_history`:

`"circulating_years"`

Reported cases are taken as evidence of whether the disease was circulating, not of how many infections there were. Transmission is on (at `R0`) in every year with at least `circulation_threshold` reported cases per million people, and in every year before reporting starts; it is off in years with fewer. A year with no report keeps the status of the year before. Pertussis is treated as circulating in every year, because it circulates everywhere whether or not it is reported. Reported cases (divided by `reporting_fraction`), and never fewer than `seed_floor` infections, are introduced on the first day of each year so that infection can return after fade-out. The number of infections is whatever the model implies. With `circulation_threshold = 0` transmission is on throughout (what `WHO_seed_switch = FALSE` meant in 0.1.0).

`"reported_cases_only"`

Case reporting and reported vaccination are taken as complete. Transmission runs at `R0` until the first year with a reported case and is switched off from then on; after that the only infections are the reported cases (divided by `reporting_fraction`), introduced on the first day of each year. This is the assumption PREVAIL 0.1.0 made, with `reporting_fraction = 1`.

Seeded infections enter the exposed compartment, placed across ages and vaccination strata in proportion to the effective number of susceptibles on the day.

`reporting_fraction` is where an estimated reporting level slots in: seeded infections are the reported cases divided by it. It can be a single number or a vector named by year (years without a name take the value of the nearest named year).
